items.title: C777 web development drill
items.summary: A second study page for the six units of the WGU C777 guide (HTML, CSS3, JavaScript, HTML APIs, forms, mobile) with about 790 questions, practice by unit, exam mode, timed runs and weak spots.

items.title: Visual header and footer editor
items.summary: Edit the header and footer on a live preview.

items.title: Study popup
items.summary: Opens filling the window, movable and resizable.

items.title: Study weak spots
items.summary: Remembers what each person misses and builds a question set from it.

items.title: Cache public pages at the edge
items.summary: Serve public HTML from Cloudflare's cache for speed.

items.title: Block inspector overhaul
items.summary: Grouped, searchable controls with per-control reset.

items.title: One button and control system
items.summary: The same buttons and controls, editable from settings, across the admin and the public site.

items.title: Admin density setting
items.summary: Compact or comfortable spacing.

items.title: Design tokens
items.summary: Shared spacing and shadow scales.

items.title: Canvas improvements
items.summary: Real block previews, a selection toolbar with an Edit button, rescaling, minimum sizes, blocks that never clip their content.

items.title: Resizable side panels and dialogs
items.summary: Drag panels to size them and hide them; dialogs resize by their sides.

items.title: Save indicators and Ctrl+S
items.summary: The same "saved" feedback in every editor; Ctrl/Cmd+S saves the one on top.

items.title: Accessibility pass
items.summary: Axe findings fixed across the admin and the public site.

items.title: Command palette
items.summary: Ctrl+K to jump to anything.

items.title: Features board
items.summary: To do on the left (bugs, things that need attention, almost-done work, ideas, decisions waiting on you), Working on now and Done on the right. You add your own requests; Claude moves items across as they are started and finished.
items.notes: Your requests live on the site: use Copy for Claude to paste the new ones into the chat so they can be picked up.

items.title: Two-factor sign-in (TOTP)
items.summary: An authenticator-app code on top of the password.
items.notes: Do you want it, and should it be asked for every sign-in or remembered per device?

items.title: Export audio (WAV)
items.summary: Sample rate, bit depth, repeats and dither.

items.title: Publish a song track to a project
Melody tools and ties
items.summary: Transpose, reverse, rotate and tie notes together.

items.title: Sign-in lockout
items.summary: Wrong passwords are counted and a connection that gets too many is locked out for a while, with a message that says how long.

items.title: Delete old Vercel deployments
items.summary: Clear the 14 deployment records the Vercel integration left on the repository. Vercel was never used.
items.notes: Needs a GitHub token with Deployments write access (the current one is read-only), and the Vercel project disconnected in Vercel's own dashboard so it stops adding new ones.

items.title: Faster node tests
items.summary: About 6 s instead of 15 s, with name filters.

items.title: Browser tests in the repo
items.summary: 58 Playwright tests, run in parallel on throwaway servers (about 3 minutes), reporting only new failures.

items.title: CLAUDE.md
items.summary: The site's layout, workflow and rules written down so every session starts fast.

items.title: Fix the remaining known-failing browser tests
items.summary: All four browser tests that were failing for old reasons now pass (the media library one no longer depends on seeded folders, the others learned about the in-page dialogs and folded sections), and two of them no longer exit 0 after printing FAIL. A full run is now clean with nothing set aside.

items.title: Pick a share picture and a fuller home page title
items.summary: Links to the site show no picture, and the home page's search title is just "Dominick".
items.notes: Two quick choices only you can make: upload a default share image in Settings > Sharing (1200 x 630 works best), and say if you want a longer home page title such as your name plus what the site is. I can write the title once you pick the wording.

items.title: Admin console quality pass
items.summary: Every admin tool, tab, editor and dropdown checked on desktop and phone in both themes. Fixed: keyboard focus lost after the Diagnostics scan and after closing a builder, unlabelled journal fields, scrolling log lists the keyboard could not reach, low-contrast accent buttons and error text in light and dark, and phone-sized tap targets and a squeezed image-address field. A new audit script re-checks all of it in about four minutes.

items.title: Song Studio
items.summary: The only way to make a song now, built for a phone first, drawn from your sketch: five fixed tracks stacked on top of each other (1 Drums, 2 Bass, 3 Chords, 4 Melody, 5 Lead) that you scroll through or tap, the open track's card with a strip of bars, Steps or a Roll to draw notes (drag to hold a note, drag to erase), play controls with volume and metronome buttons that pop up their sliders, and a piano that stays at the bottom. A Tools sheet holds everything else the old editor could do: each track's sound and its shape (attack, release, brightness, vibrato and more), the track tools, the song's settings, patterns and song order, the player look and every export. Songs are stored as before.

items.title: Song length, track loops and free recording
items.summary: A song has a number of bars (or grows as you record) and every track has its own strip of bars: a two-bar drum beat can loop under everything while you record a melody for as long as you like, a bar can be made different from the ones it repeats, and Loop can be turned off per track. Up to 16 patterns and 64 bars. The public player, audio, stems and MIDI file follow it.

items.title: Free or scale-snapped notes, sound shaping, MIDI keyboard, default tempo
items.summary: Notes are free by default; pick a scale and turn on Snap and what you play or tap moves to the nearest note of it. Every melodic track can shape its sound (attack, decay, sustain, release, brightness, thickness, vibrato, wave) and the tweaks are saved with the song. A MIDI keyboard connects from the top bar (and reconnects by itself); on Drums its pads play and record the drum sounds. Site Settings has a Songs tab for the tempo, length and drum kit a new song starts with.

items.title: Song module upgrades
items.summary: Better melody instruments, more drum sounds, echo, chord progressions, and several patterns chained into a full song, all shipped one by one. Old songs sound exactly the same.

items.title: Melody instruments
items.summary: Pick Pluck, Lead, Pad, Bass or Bell for the melody; each shapes the note with its own attack, release and filter. Old songs keep their plain sound.

items.title: Held notes survive import and MIDI export
items.summary: Importing a song file used to drop its held (tied) notes, and the MIDI file wrote them as separate short notes. Both now keep them as one long note.

items.title: More drum sounds
items.summary: Open hat, rim, tom and crash in all three kits, added from a menu under the grid and removed with the ×. A closed hat cuts a ringing open hat. Three new starter beats use them. They export to MIDI, stems and song files.

items.title: Echo
items.summary: A tempo-synced echo slider next to Space: repeats a dotted eighth later, each one quieter and duller. Off by default, in exports and on the public player.

items.title: Chord progressions
items.summary: Stamp a whole progression (pop, doo-wop, jazz, minor, Andalusian, canon and more) in any key across the loop, held so the chords ring, in one undo step. The key follows the highlighted scale.

items.title: Import a MIDI file
items.summary: Songs list → Import MIDI…: drums land on the drum rows, the busiest other part becomes the melody (moved by octaves to fit, long notes tied), and each bar becomes a pattern with a song order. It makes a new song and tells you what could not be kept (tempo changes, other time signatures, unknown drums, extra parts, bars past 32). Export MIDI now writes the whole song order too.

items.title: Bar counter on the player
items.summary: A song with a song order now says "6 bars" at rest and "Bar 3 of 6" while it plays, with a thin segment per bar (done, now, to come). The builder's preview shows the same plus the pattern letter. One-bar songs show nothing.

items.title: Bass line
items.summary: A second part under the melody: press Bass above the piano roll for its own low roll (C1 to B2), bass sound (or pluck, lead, pad, bell), volume, mute and hide. It has its own notes in every pattern, the same shift, reverse, random, tie, arpeggio and transpose tools, chord roots from a progression, and Follow the kick. It plays on the public player, in the audio and stems, in the MIDI file (own track, channel 2) and in the report. Importing a MIDI file puts a part named Bass, or one below C3, on it. Songs that never use it are unchanged.

items.title: Starter songs
items.summary: The New song menu now lists four complete little songs to start from or learn from: Lo-fi loop, Four on the floor, Funk groove and Dark trap. Each has patterns, a song order, a melody, a bass line and mix settings, with notes on how it is built.

items.title: Move bars in the song order, [ and ] for patterns
items.summary: Every bar in the song order has Earlier and Later buttons, so a pattern can go anywhere (add it, then move it). While editing, [ and ] open the previous and next pattern.

items.title: Pump
items.summary: A Pump slider next to Echo: the music (melody, bass, chords and lead) dips on every kick and swells back, like sidechain compression, so the groove breathes. Off by default; it is in the audio export, the waveform and on the public player. The house starter uses it.

items.title: Drum fills, and copy a part from another pattern
items.summary: Add fill changes the end of a bar into a snare roll, snare build, tom run, kick-and-snare drive or a drop-out. In a song with several patterns, Copy here takes the drums, melody, bass line or everything from another pattern into the open one.

items.title: Patterns and song order
items.summary: Up to four patterns (A to D) per song, switched with buttons, copied or removed, and a song order (like A A B A C) that plays them one after another. Play can follow the order or loop the pattern you're editing. The public player, the waveform, audio and stem export and the MIDI file all cover the whole song. Old songs are untouched.

items.title: More sounds, deeper sound editing, recording helpers
items.summary: Over forty instruments in six groups and fifteen drum kits. The Sound tab now has an envelope, a filter (type, brightness, resonance, sweep), tone (voices, thickness, sub, noise, drive, FM) and movement (vibrato and tremolo, with speeds), and each drum sound has its own tune, length and tone. Preview works on every sound, and Play and Preview no longer go silent on a phone that was keeping the sound asleep. Next to Rec: a button that always records from the beginning, Quantize (nearest step, eighth or beat) and a Follow switch for the editor.

items.title: Blocks look the same wherever they are placed
items.summary: A block is exactly its content: no stray outer margins from paragraphs, headings or rules, so the space between blocks is the same for every kind, 16px on a phone and 8px on a wide screen. A spacer keeps its height on a phone (it used to vanish), and nothing runs past the screen edge.

items.title: Studio has its own page and nav tab
items.summary: The Studio is now a page of its own, /studio, with a Studio tab in the nav, open to everyone. The song builder fills the page; visitors make songs that are kept in their own browser (nothing is sent to the site), and can save and share song files. It follows the site's light and dark.

items.title: The admin opens on the page: click where you want a block
items.summary: The admin opens on the page itself with the page chooser and + Add in the top bar. Click an empty spot on the page and pick a block: it lands right there (pushing what is below it down). A selected block has Size (a quarter to full width, left, centre or right), Settings and Edit in its toolbar. The menu and the inspector stay tucked away until you ask: Tools and Settings.

items.title: Page editor: the rest of the Squarespace feel
items.summary: Next: blocks in the editor that look exactly like the live page, insert bars between blocks on a phone, and folding the inspector into the selection bar.
items.notes: Tell me what feels off in the new click-to-add flow and I will fix that first.

items.title: One chunky look for every button and field
items.summary: Buttons are now a thick outline with a flat fill and a hard shadow they sink into when pressed, on the site, in the admin and in the Studio. Text fields have the same thick outline, and a labelled field can carry its label in the outline. Site Settings > Buttons & controls has a Chunky choice (the new default) next to the old looks.

items.title: No emoji anywhere on the site
items.summary: Every emoji is gone, on the public site and in the admin: the reactions are drawn icons (thumbs up, light bulb, heart), Read aloud and the song player's Play and Stop have drawn icons, external links have a drawn arrow, and the warnings, tool buttons and simulator messages use plain words. Symbols a phone turns into emoji (play, stop, the corner arrow) count too. A test now fails if one ever comes back.

items.title: The nav's ticks line up under every tab
items.summary: The ruler under the tabs is drawn from the tabs themselves: a long tick under the middle of each one and five short ticks evenly between, on a phone (including when the bar scrolls sideways with all the tabs) and on a computer. The orange needle always lands on its tab's tick, and the ticks move with the tabs when you scroll the bar.

items.title: All the nav tabs fit on a phone
items.summary: The tabs are a little snugger and the bar runs nearly edge to edge on a phone, so Home, Studio, PicEditor, Simulations, Scans and Search all show without scrolling on a standard iPhone. The fade at the edge of the bar now only shows when there really is more to scroll to.

items.title: The Studio runs on the same base as PicEditor, Simulations and Scans
items.summary: Behind the scenes the Studio page now shares its loading, styling and tab-switching code with the other three tool pages, so all four open, park and come back the same way and a fix to one reaches all four. Nothing changes in what you see (checked pixel for pixel) or in the songs saved in your browser. One small thing: the main button on the other three tool pages now has the same press-down look as every other button on the site.

items.title: Editing a block with a pill bar
items.summary: Select a block and its controls float at the bottom of the editor as soft pills, from your sketch: + adds a setting (background, padding, corners, shadow, animation and more), a chip for the block opens its text, a chip for its width, a chip for each thing it has set that you tap to change or × to take off, a dropdown pill for its main choice (a heading's level), ⋯ for copy, duplicate, lock, fit and delete, and a round Done. In your site's accent colour, and on a phone too.

items.title: Tabs switch with no wait, and no site name in the header
items.summary: Every page of the nav is kept once it has been fetched, so a tab shows straight away and a fresh copy is fetched quietly in the background. The Studio's editor is fetched ahead of time too, so the Studio tab opens without loading. The header is just the nav dial now, centred.

items.title: The Studio is part of the site, not the admin's editor on top
items.summary: /studio opens on a shelf of your songs: New song, the starter songs, opening a song or MIDI file, and a card per song with a little picture of its tracks, a Play button right on the card, Copy and Delete. The editor opens right there under the site's nav, in the site's look, with no frame or dialog around it; Songs takes you back to the shelf and keeps what you did. Switching to another tab and back slides in place and the song you had open is still open.

items.title: Studio: the ⋯ controls as a row, quantize shows its value
items.summary: Holding Rec (or the ⋯) lays a row of buttons over the play bar instead of a half circle over the steps, without labels. Quantize shows 1/16, 1/8, 1/4 or Off and a tap moves to the next.

items.title: The Studio is no longer crammed on a phone
items.summary: The five tracks are one row of tabs, the open track has one row of controls, the steps or roll fill the rest of the screen (half a bar of drum steps at a time with a pager), and Play, Stop, Undo, Rec and the keys are always in reach. The fan has names under its circles, the Tools sheet has its own Play button, a phone on its side gets two columns, and a wide screen shows the tracks as a rail. A new song on /studio is kept from its first change.

items.title: Nav dial: turn it like a camera dial
items.summary: The stop you are on sits under a needle in the middle and is the biggest; the others step down in size on both sides like a staircase. On a phone you drag the dial and, as it settles on a stop, that page comes in; on a computer you click the stop you want and it turns to the middle. Home starts in the middle with stops either side, names are lowercase, Simulations is called Sim, and Search opens the finder when the dial lands on it (or when you press it).

items.title: Studio on a wide screen: the whole page, songs on the left, sound on the right
items.summary: On a computer the Studio takes the whole view. A panel on the left lists your songs so you can switch between them without leaving the editor (it saves the one you are on first), and a panel on the right is the open track's sound: browse the instruments or drum kits by group, pick one to hear it, and turn the dials to shape it. Either panel folds away to give the music the full width.

items.title: A better step sequencer and piano roll
items.summary: Drum steps paint by dragging across them (and across rows), with a lane of bars under the grid to set how hard each hit is. In the roll you drag a note to move it (along and up or down), pull its right edge to resize it, Alt-drag to copy it, Shift-drag a box to pick several, then nudge them with the arrow keys or delete them. There is a strength lane, a snap setting (1/16, 1/8, 1/4), zoom, the other tracks' notes as faint ghosts, and shift, copy and paste for a bar.

items.title: Drag the page with a mouse to switch tabs
items.summary: On a computer you can now press on an empty part of a page and drag hard sideways to move to the tab beside it, like the swipe on a phone. Pull past a quarter of the way (or flick) and it goes; let go sooner and it springs back. Selecting text, links and controls still work as before.

items.title: Studio keys: hold them, bend them, arpeggiate, strum, roll the pads
items.summary: Every key now carries its name (the C of each octave is marked, black keys read C#, D# and so on) and the keys look like keys. Press and hold a key and the note sounds for as long as you hold it; with Rec on, a held key is recorded as one long note. A Hold button keeps notes (and pad rolls) going after you let go, and a pitch wheel beside the keys bends what you hold and springs back. The Play button changes how the keys play: Arpeggio (up, down, up and down, as played, over one to three octaves, at 1/4 to a 1/32 roll), Strum (a chord on the key, major, minor, seventh and more, fast or slow, down, up or alternating) and Random (random notes from the keys you hold). The drum pads hit harder the lower on the pad you press (a pen uses its pressure), and with Roll on, holding a pad repeats it for hi-hat rolls, with an optional swell. On a phone, Tools is now a dropdown under its button instead of a full screen.

items.title: Preview pictures for sharing
items.summary: Each tool page and the site itself now have a share picture, so links look right in messages and social posts.

items.title: Studio first-time tip
items.summary: The first time someone opens the Studio, a short tip explains the keys, Hold and the Rec button. It shows once.

items.title: MIDI tab in the Studio tools
items.summary: Tools has a new MIDI tab: connect your keyboard, see its name listed, then press keys and watch each one show up (note, velocity, pedal) on a 37-key strip. It tells you if the browser blocks MIDI or no keyboard is found, and whether a note is inside the open track range so it records.

items.title: Tracks like a DAW playlist
items.summary: The five tracks are now rows like FL Studio: a header on the left (number, name, mute) and the song bars as clips on a timeline you can scroll sideways, with a ruler and a line that follows the music. Tap a clip to edit that track in that bar. The order and the five tracks are the same as before. On a short screen the rows scroll so the editor keeps its room.

items.title: Fold the open track, resize it on a phone
items.summary: The open track has a fold button: it shrinks to its one row of controls and the tracks above grow taller. On a phone there is also a handle between the tracks and the open track: drag it up or down to choose how tall the open track is (double tap puts it back). Both are remembered in the browser.

items.title: The plugin-aggregate look across the site and admin
items.summary: Pages, tool pages and the admin take the look of the plugin-aggregate app: near-black surfaces, cyan and magenta accents, IBM Plex Mono everywhere, flat 1px outlines with small corners. The Studio takes the aggregate DAW's colours for its five tracks and a faint grid in the playlist. The nav and the finder keep their old look.

items.title: Cassette colours, the new nav and the reorganised Studio
items.summary: The site is in the Cassette colours (navy, orange, soft blue; a light version too). The nav is three icons on a lens scale with a sliding needle and DOMINICK.DOMINICK behind it. The Studio has one display bar at the top with every switch named, the tools docked as an inspector on a computer and as a bottom deck with a dial on a phone, and no hidden fan.

items.title: Bit bento look with an orange accent
items.summary: The public site, the Studio and the admin are in the Bit bento look: black and white with a dither, Mac-style windows with title bars and close boxes, pixel type, 1-bit icons, and a small touch of orange for the playhead, record, focus and the lit dial tick. The dark theme is the light one inverted. The nav keeps the dial but its stops no longer change size. Not built yet from the mockup: the now-playing, songs, Look and Find tiles and the pinned player on Home.

items.title: Site cut down to Home and Studio
items.summary: The site is now a home page with two study buttons, and the Studio. Search, articles, projects, the circuit simulator, scans, the photo editor, the aim trainer, hidden notes, scripts, analytics and the rest were deleted from the code. The admin only edits the home page.
items.notes: The old code is in the git tag before-slim-down. The database tables of the deleted features are untouched.

items.title: Softer colours that are easier on the eyes
items.summary: Warm cream paper with charcoal ink in the light theme, soft charcoal paper with warm off-white ink in the dark theme, and a faint dot ground instead of hard lines. Contrast is about 12:1, down from 21:1.

items.title: Settings dialog instead of the finder
items.summary: The last stop of the nav opens a small dialog with light or dark, reduce motion, text size and links to the pages. The search box is gone.

items.title: Production pipeline
items.summary: A pull request is checked and previewed. A push to main is checked, then deployed only if the checks are green, smoke-tested and rolled back if that fails. Database migrations only run when asked and typed in. The live site is smoke-tested every six hours.
items.notes: To finish: add CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID as repository secrets, then switch off Cloudflare's own git build for main so it is not deployed twice. Until then the deploy steps skip and Cloudflare's build keeps deploying. Branch protection is not available on a free private repository.

items.title: Clean commit history
items.summary: Every commit message is a plain bulleted list of the changes, with no attribution lines or session links, and every commit is under your name.

items.title: Both study modules on the home page
items.summary: The home page has a button for the A+ Core 1 drill and one for the C777 web development drill. Each asks for the password before it opens.
items.notes: Set a STUDY_PASSWORD secret on the Worker: without one the password is the built-in default.

items.title: Old branches deleted
items.summary: The production branch and three old working branches were deleted; everything in them was already in main. main is the only branch.

items.title: Webhook alerts removed
items.summary: The alerts for repeated wrong passwords and for a failed daily backup were removed with the webhook settings, since nothing could switch them on. A failed backup is still shown in the admin and written to the error log.

items.title: The Studio has its own files
items.summary: The Studio no longer fetches the admin's page and stylesheet. Its dialogs, scripts and stylesheet live in public/studio, the admin is 180 KB lighter, and the first visit downloads its scripts in parallel instead of one after another.

items.title: A limiter so loud mixes do not clip
items.summary: A soft limiter sits in front of the speakers: a normal mix is untouched, and a pile-up of pads, chords and drums is squashed gently instead of clipping into harsh distortion. The audio export is limited too.

items.title: Steadier playback on busy phones
items.summary: When a phone is too busy to keep time, the Studio now skips the steps it missed instead of playing them in a burst, looks further ahead for a while, and wakes the sound again after a call or a switch of app. The echo no longer clicks when the tempo changes.

items.title: Recorded notes land where you played them
items.summary: Recording now allows for the delay between the sound being made and being heard (a phone speaker, a Bluetooth headset) and uses the keyboard's own timing, so a note you tap on the beat is written on the beat.

items.title: Drag the playlist and open track to any height, with a magnet
items.summary: The handle between the playlist and the open track now works on wide screens as well as phones. Drag it up or down; it snaps to useful heights (shortest, the playlist showing all five tracks, tallest, automatic) and lights up when it does. Hold Alt to drag freely.

items.title: A more readable text font
items.summary: Text across the site and the Studio is now JetBrains Mono instead of the thin pixel font, which is easier on the eyes. Small labels and title bars stay in the pixel font, and so do the big position and tempo digits.

items.title: A calmer look
items.summary: Home page blocks no longer carry an empty striped title bar, the background is one flat tone instead of dots, the small pixel labels are a little bigger, and only the open song is filled in on the Studio's song list (hovering another is a light tint).

items.title: Roomier tabs and bigger touch targets
items.summary: The Studio's tabs have room to breathe and scroll sideways when they do not fit, with the open one kept in view. On a phone the playlist mute buttons, the tabs and the toggles are 40 pixels tall. The phone nav shows SETTINGS in full.

items.title: A clearer top of the Studio
items.summary: Play is the biggest control and the position and tempo digits are larger, so the top of the Studio has an obvious place to look. The home page title is larger and the sample home page now has a line about the site and an Open the Studio button.

items.title: A simpler Sound panel
items.summary: Volume, Preview and Mute stay at the top of the Sound panel while you scroll. The knobs show one part of the sound at a time (Envelope, Filter, Tone, Movement), and for drums the sounds and their knobs come first, with the kit and the extras folded away.

items.title: Swipe between the Studio sections on a phone
items.summary: On a phone, the sections under the Studio (pads, sound, track, song, patterns, share, midi) are a row you scroll sideways like the nav dial. The one in the middle is the one shown, and it switches when you stop scrolling. A tap scrolls a section to the middle.

items.title: A more reliable Studio on phones
items.summary: A phone held on its side shows the whole Studio again (the playlist and editor had been squeezed to a few pixels), the smallest phones keep Undo and the position and tempo in view, opening the Studio no longer scrolls its top under the menu, touch targets are bigger, and a phone test now checks five sizes in light and dark.

items.title: Precise dials
items.summary: Every dial now shows its value in its own unit while you turn it, turns four times finer with Shift (or a held press on a phone) without jumping, answers arrow keys, PageUp and PageDown, and the wheel, goes back to the sound's own value on a double-click, and lets you type an exact value. Volumes read in decibels, round values pull the dial gently, and short attacks keep their precision.

items.title: Hear the sound while you turn a knob
items.summary: Press a dial in the Sound panel and a note is held while you turn it, following the knob (filter, vibrato, tremolo, sub, detune, FM, drive, release), so you can judge a sound by ear as it changes. Drum dials replay their drum as they move. Typing a tempo no longer drops the song to 1 BPM on the way to 120, and the pump and echo no longer click.

items.title: Play with feeling
items.summary: Piano keys sound harder the lower on the key you press, a MIDI keyboard's notes are held for as long as the key is down (with its own strength, the sustain pedal, the pitch wheel, the mod wheel for vibrato and CC 74 for brightness), and the computer keyboard holds notes and shifts octave with the comma and full stop keys.

items.title: A mixer with pan and solo, and stereo export
items.summary: The Song pane has a mixer: a level and a pan for each of the five tracks and a Solo to hear one track alone. Panned tracks move across the speakers, and the audio export is now stereo by default (mono is still a choice).

items.title: Drums that sound like drums
items.summary: Every drum was rebuilt: kicks fall fast onto a note and have a beater click, snares have a two-part shell with wires and a crack, hats and cymbals are metallic instead of hiss, claps have several hands and a room tail, and a harder hit is brighter as well as louder. No two hits are quite the same.

items.title: Just the Studio and a search
items.summary: The home page is gone: the address of the site opens the Studio. The nav is the Studio and a magnifier that opens a search and command dialog (also Ctrl or Cmd with K): type to find a setting, and type a study module's name to open it (it still asks for its password).
